// What this is: The COMPLETE local-development configuration surface for TfLens, in ONE place (REQ-NFR-011). Every setting the app reads is listed below, secret or not. Anything you leave out falls back to the default given in its comment — so you can run TfLens with an empty secrets.json, and you never have to hunt through code, .env and appsettings to find out what is configurable.
// How to use: In Visual Studio, right-click the TfLens project > Manage User Secrets. That opens YOUR private secrets.json (outside the repository). Paste the block below into it and fill in only what you need to change.
// Precedence: environment variables  >  user secrets  >  the code defaults noted below. A launch profile sets an environment variable, so it silently beats your user secrets — do not put settings there.
// Note: This is the LOCAL DEVELOPMENT (F5 / dotnet run) path only. Deployment supplies the SAME settings as PascalCase environment variables — see .env.example and docker-compose.yml. Nothing in Program.cs parses .env; that file belongs to docker compose.
// TfLens:DbConnection: REQUIRED, in every environment including Development. Npgsql connection string, e.g. Host=localhost;Port=5550;Database=tflens;Username=<user>;Password=<password>. There is NO default: as of 2026-08-29 the source-side Development fallback was removed (it held a password in committed code AND silently pinned every unconfigured developer to one specific database — see MISS-TfLens-20260829-23). Point this at the PostgreSQL server you already run. TfLens does not start a database for you.
// TfLens:AppManagerApiKey: REQUIRED, and required TOGETHER with the secret below — whole or not at all (DECISIONS.md D-006). A half-configured or wrong pair returns 401 INVALID_API_KEY on every call, so startup refuses it. Password reset cannot work at all unconfigured: /AuthSvc/forgot-password and /AuthSvc/reset-password take the app scope only from this header pair.
// TfLens:AppManagerApiSecret: REQUIRED with the key above. See D-006.
// TfLens:AppManagerAppId: REQUIRED as of 2026-08-29. The ApplicationId TfLens sends in every AppManager request body; TfLens is application 1. It no longer defaults in source, because which application accepts your users is a property of the deployment — a wrong-but-present default sends real credentials to the wrong application and surfaces as an opaque 401 instead of a configuration error. docker-compose.yml sets TfLensAppManagerAppId explicitly, so deployment is unaffected.
// TfLens:GitHubToken: OPTIONAL. A PAT raises the rate limit from 60/hour to 5,000/hour. It grants NO access a public request would not have — TfLens refuses private repos regardless (REQ-FN-015). In practice a sync of several repos needs it.
// TfLens:DataRoot: OPTIONAL. Where raw/, reports/ and prices.json live. Default when unset: data (relative to the working directory).
// TfLens:PollIntervalMinutes: OPTIONAL. Background repository poll interval. Default when unset: 15.
// TfLens:StalenessDays: OPTIONAL. Drives the Coverage staleness warning. Default when unset: 7.
